title: Built a small Flappy Bird-style game with AI in a few hours, including the assets
author: CapyArchitect
selftext:
I spent a few hours building a small Flappy Bird-style browser game with AI, and it ended up more polished than I expected.

The build included:

\- generated art/assets

\- core gameplay loop

\- collision + scoring

\- restart flow

\- saving the player’s highest score

\- a leaderboard

It’s still a small web game, but getting from idea to something playable this quickly feels wild.

https://reddit.com/link/1tu69j3/video/y8xcsuufnq4h1/player

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
It looks cute and you intentionally choose a simple style that works well imo

I think flappy bird and infinite runners are like snakes and pong games for this current generation of gamedev

replies.author: CapyArchitect
replies.body:
Thank you! I’m glad the style works. I wanted to keep it simple and cute, but still make it feel polished enough to be fun.

And yeah, I totally agree. Flappy Bird/infinite runners feel like the modern Pong or Snake: small scope, easy to understand, but still a great way to start experiment new tools.

comments.author: Fluid_Genius
comments.body: Very cute. Was this done in codex?

replies.author: CapyArchitect
replies.body: Yes. I used codex to generate the assets and code

comments.author: fued
comments.body:
playable sure. it is maybe 10% the way to a released product tho, it needs so much work.

ai is good for tech demos, it cant make games yet

replies.author: CapyArchitect
replies.body: I agree. Specially when you want add ADs, user sign in, cloud storage etc.

replies.author: fued
replies.body:
AI isnt too bad at that stuff, im thinking more player controls, getting good music that fits it, making sure difficulty is good, making sure player engagement stays etc.

all the things that cant be measured easily and require a heap of playtesting
